leads.work: Shippers email Transwestern to change a contract (raise MDQ for one or two days, extend the term, assign receipt points, continue last month's terms). The account director replies 'Approved' and forwards each request to Dennis Lee or Michael Bodnar, who draft an amendment and update the admin contract.
leads.why: Julie Reames at BR sent same-day 'increase contract 27748' requests on 12/10, 12/10 (for 12/11), 12/11 and 12/13. The same pattern shows up with Western Gas, TMV, Reliant and PPL. Each one is a phone call, then an email, then a forward, then a manual amendment. Some are re-forwarded as FYI, and PPL needed several amendments (#3, #4) with mix-ups over which version was signed.

leads.work: A weekly California Capacity Report is typed by hand into an email: TW and El Paso deliveries and utilization percentages, Gas Daily prices and Enron basis.
leads.why: The same template went out every Friday for 12/10, 12/17, 12/26, 12/31 and 01/07. An old email was copied forward and a correction had to follow because the week label was wrong. The data comes from systems and could be produced automatically.

leads.work: Credit approval requests and a daily contract status list (processing, tendered, terminating) are broadcast by email to large distribution lists.
leads.why: These are formatted, repeated status notices for each contract and each day ('December 1st Contract Status as of November 27th at 4:50 pm', 'Credit Approval Requested'). The workflow and status could be tracked in a system instead.

leads.work: Handling power schedule cuts on the Portland real-time desk: paper cut sheets, zeroing deals in Enpower, building 1 MW annuities by hand to carry the cut value, notes in path confirmation, and filing everything in an accordion folder.
leads.why: The manager sent several changing procedure emails ('Cuts are on the way', 'More CUTS procedures', a refined cut technique). He wrote that the desk was 'having a nightmare taking care of weekend cuts', that the cuts database threw errors, and that Enron was trying to reconcile each counterparty's cuts from the paper sheets.

leads.work: An average price spreadsheet (SchedulePull.xls) that queries Enpower hourly deals by region, and the many rounds needed to get its exclusion rules right.
leads.why: From 11/21 to 12/07 there were repeated fixes: averaging per deal instead of per MW, transmission, California Imbalance, EPMI Cal Pool and annuity deals to exclude, no data for early November, and the archive version running too slowly. Kate Symes was apparently computing these averages by hand before. A Dow Jones price sheet was also mentioned.

leads.work: El Paso Electric (EPE) service: the daily EPE model emailed to EPE, hourly deal sheets kept in a paper binder as the source for settlements, and shift notes on unit trips and resupply.
leads.why: A deal sheet for 12/30 to 1/1 went missing and had to be rebuilt. The model is sent every day (12/25, 12/28, 1/10). Procedure updates were forwarded by email and then turned out to be wrong.

leads.work: Requesting and approving system access by email: Enpower access requests that went to the wrong approver, Global Trader IDs, RiskTrac access, Netco book requests and the risk/desk access matrix.
leads.why: Nine ARSystem approval requests went to someone who was not the approver and had to be forwarded on. Book request forms (one xls per region) and the matrix were revised several times.

leads.work: Netco/UBS setup in the risk group: spreadsheet-driven curve lists, Sitara curve mappings, a trader-book matrix, EOL product-to-trader mappings, regional P&L files, and repointing macros that use ERMS spreadsheets.
leads.why: Kam Keiser sent a stream of 'please update file X on the O drive' requests. The EOL product mapping was redone a second time. Many hard-coded spreadsheet paths and macros had to be changed. This shows a heavy dependence on spreadsheets.

leads.work: Correcting counterparty and deal data so old payments can be released. In this case a deal's counterparty name had to change to Black Marlin Pipeline Company Inc.
leads.why: The request bounced between Volume Management, logistics, Global Contracts and another group for almost two weeks, with repeated chasers ('Have you had a chance...'), while payments were held up.

leads.work: Entering and pathing deals after the fact for accounting close: the Centana storage sale to AEP needed old contracts reactivated, and Unify volumes had to be reconciled against the GL.
leads.why: This ran from 11/13 to 12/12 with many chasers to get it done before close, a gap between Unify and GL volumes, and Global Counterparties having to reactivate contracts.

leads.work: Bulk changes to deals in Sitara: killing or zeroing about 2000 desk-to-desk deals, and moving auto-terminated deals into the bankruptcy book, sent out in numbered parts.
leads.why: There was confusion between killing and zeroing deals and a worry that Volume Management would have to zero 2000 deals by hand. Contracts sent the deal lists piecemeal ('part 3', 'part 4'), and logistics had to check by hand whether volumes flowed after 11/30.

leads.work: An assistant chases the team for time and vacation reports by email every period.
leads.why: 'Time Reports Are Due!!!' was sent to the whole team and led to back-and-forth replies about half days. It came round again on 1/3.

leads.work: Creating DA/HA final reports in CAPS. SQL errors force a manual sequence: import, create, check load zones, and pull missing hours one at a time.
leads.why: The manager sent instructions for working around the recurring failures. Schedule errors, such as a wrong import ID or a DA schedule moved to HA, also needed manual fixes to load zones and templates.

leads.work: Shift handover and incident write-ups by email, along with pulling recorded call tapes to settle disputes with counterparties (SRP, LADWP).
leads.why: There were several narrative incident emails each week, and tape pulls were requested over disputed trades. A detailed daily activity recap of trades was also written by hand for the gas desk.

leads.work: Tracking shift schedule changes and swaps.
leads.why: Off-schedule swaps had to be tracked through calls and emails to the manager, and a new monthly schedule is kept in a notebook.

leads.work: Managing shared logins and passwords by email: vendor (OATI) password changes requested by email, and a new ISO password broadcast in plain text.
leads.why: Credentials are rotated by hand and sent out over email.

leads.work: Expense report and invoice processing: approvals pending in XMS and iPayIt, and a manual review of pre-petition expenses over $5k.
leads.why: Bowen's notice says the review will be 'a manual process' that 'will take some time' and asks employees to send summaries by email. Users were also told to clear open items by a deadline, and Concur sends automatic status emails.

leads.work: Tracking cash from OBA imbalance settlements and confirming wire receipts.
leads.why: Williams Field Services' imbalance cash-out was followed through several emails to Corman, Harris, Accounting and Tax, and a separate TW imbalance meeting and imbalance spreadsheet were sent out.

leads.work: Missing trade confirmations for forward gas deals, which then turn into closeout or settlement talks.
leads.why: Great River Energy never received a confirmation for a May to July purchase and asked whether Enron would stand behind it, then asked for a closeout.

leads.work: Investigating GL write-offs and reconciliation differences at month-end.
leads.why: A potential write-off spreadsheet was forwarded to several people to trace the differences, and Lisa Koerselman said the approval chain was unclear.

leads.work: Setting up new EOL points and combinations, with long boilerplate product description text pasted in each time.
leads.why: A request is made by email for every new transport product, with the GTC legal text and XXX/yyy placeholders filled in by hand.

leads.work: Daily IDs emailed between staff (prompt post IDs for each region).
leads.why: Lists of ID numbers sent by email, apparently every day.

leads.work: Coordinating Enpower database outages and test-deal entry for the Netco/Estate split, and testing the FSP system.
leads.why: Outage approval was gathered over email, test deals were handed from shift to shift, and users were asked to test the FSP release.

leads.work: HR asking employees to check their home contact data by email, and a change to payroll deductions requested by email.
leads.why: Each employee got a personal 'reply if incorrect' email. The United Way deduction was stopped through an email chain.
